title: Trash flies as Ole Miss fans rage over controversial calls vs. Georgia

 Zac Al-Khateeb USA TODAY Nov. 7, 2026, 9:32 p.m. ET Hear this story Stop us if you've heard this before: Fans disgusted by questionable calls in a high-profile game vs. Georgia are throwing trash onto the field .
 During the first half of No. 12 Mississippi's home game vs. visiting, second-ranked Georgia, a pair of officiating decisions resulted in Ole Miss fans losing their temper — and throwing objects onto the field .
 The first of those occurred in the 11-minute mark of the second quarter with Ole Miss already trailing 21-0. A roughing the passer penalty on defensive end Jordan Renaud wiped off a Gunner Stockton interception, allowing the Bulldogs to continue their drive (which ultimately ended with a punt).
 Roughly 6:30 minutes of game clock later, Ole Miss fans again threw trash onto the field after a Jaylon Braxton defensive pass interference call extended another Georgia drive after the 3rd-and-3 play. This time, Ole Miss fans were so incensed they threw enough trash onto the field to warrant a game delay to clear debris from the field.
 Georgia later went on to add injury to insult, finishing the drive with a fourth first-half touchdown to take a 28-0 lead into halftime. Georgia had a chance for another field goal to end the half, but Peyton Woodring's 49-yard attempt was no good.
